results.name: Kneeling Wrist Flexor Stretch
instructions: Begin in a tabletop position on the floor with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Rotate your hands so that your fingers are pointing towards your knees, palms flat on the floor.
Slowly shift your weight back towards your heels to increase the stretch in your wrists and forearms, keeping your palms flat on the floor.

Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Release the stretch by shifting your weight forward and gently lifting your hands off the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your palms flat on the floor and your fingers pointing towards your knees to maximize the stretch in your wrist flexors.
Move slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain.
If the stretch is too intense, reduce the angle by bringing your hands closer to your knees.
results.description: Kneeling Wrist Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Lats Stretch Elbow on Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place one elbow on it above your head.
Step back slightly and lower your chest toward the floor.
Push your hips back until you feel a stretch along the side of your back.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your back flat.
Breathe into the stretch.
results.description: Lats Stretch Elbow on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Lats Stretch on Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place both hands on it at shoulder height or higher.
Walk your feet back and hinge at your hips.
Lower your chest toward the floor until you feel a stretch under your arms.
Hold and breathe.
tips: Keep your arms straight.
Push your hips back.
results.description: Lats Stretch on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Chest.

results.name: Leg Extended Stretch on Bench
instructions: Begin by sitting on the edge of a bench with both legs bent and your feet flat on the floor. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Extend your right leg forward until it is parallel to the floor, keeping your leg straight.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your hamstring and lower back.
Slowly bring your right leg back to the starting position with both feet flat on the floor. Repeat the stretch with your left leg extended. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your extended leg is straight and parallel to the floor to get the most effective stretch.
Perform the stretch on a stable, non-slip surface to prevent discomfort or injury.
If you find it difficult to hold your leg up, you can use your hands to support your thigh.
results.description: Leg Extended Stretch on Bench is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Glutes.

results.name: Legs Hand Reach Spine Stretch
instructions: Begin by sitting on the floor with your legs extended straight together in front of you. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Slowly bend forward at the hips, reaching your hands towards your feet. Keep your legs straight and your toes pointing up.
Continue to reach forward, aiming to touch your toes or go as far as your flexibility allows. Allow your head and neck to relax as you stretch.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily.
tips: Allow your head and neck to relax completely to maximize the stretch in your spine.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable, non-slip surface to prevent slipping or discomfort.
If you find it difficult to reach your toes, use a yoga strap or towel around your feet to assist.
results.description: Legs Hand Reach Spine Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Calves.

results.name: Lunging Straight Leg Calf Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Step your right foot back into a lunge position, keeping your right leg straight and your heel on the floor. Bend your left knee slightly, keeping your left foot flat on the floor.
Lean forward slightly, pressing your hips downward and feeling the stretch in your right calf. Hold this position for 15-30 seconds.
Return to the starting position and switch legs, stepping your left foot back and repeating the stretch.
tips: Ensure your back leg remains straight and your heel stays on the floor to maximize the stretch in your calf.
Keep your front knee aligned with your ankle to avoid unnecessary strain on your joints.
Perform the stretch on a stable, non-slip surface to prevent slipping or discomfort.
results.description: Lunging Straight Leg Calf Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

results.name: Lying (Prone) Abdominal Stretch
instructions: Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed under your shoulders, palms flat on the floor.
Slowly press your hands into the floor to lift your chest upward, extending your spine. Keep your hips and legs relaxed on the floor.
Continue to lift your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch in your abdomen and lower back. Hold this position for 15-30 seconds, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Slowly lower your chest back down to the floor and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid locking your elbows; keep them slightly bent to prevent strain on your joints.
Breathe deeply and steadily, inhaling as you lift your chest and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable surface, such as a yoga mat, to prevent discomfort or injury.
results.description: Lying (Prone) Abdominal Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Lying Bent Knee Cross Glutes Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Pull the lower leg toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the glute of the crossed leg.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Push the crossed knee away gently for more stretch.
results.description: Lying Bent Knee Cross Glutes Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Lying Crossover Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended straight and your arms out to the sides to form a T shape.
Bend and lift your right leg and cross it over your body, aiming to touch the floor on the left side, and extend your left arm to hold your right knee down.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your lower back and hips.
Slowly return your right leg to the starting position. Repeat the stretch with your left leg, crossing it over your body to the right side. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain.
Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you lift your leg and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
Avoid forcing your leg to touch the floor if you feel any pain; go as far as your flexibility allows.
results.description: Lying Crossover Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Obliques.

results.name: Lying Face Down Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Lie face down on the floor.
Bend one knee and reach back to hold your ankle or foot.
Gently pull your heel toward your glute until you feel a stretch in the front of your thigh.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips pressed into the floor.
Use a strap if you can't reach your foot.
results.description: Lying Face Down Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.
